title: Tunable periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in non-Hermitian IAAF model
abstract: Cascade of delocalization transitions provides a route to multi-step control of delocalization, yet achieving a programmable periodic cascade remains a challenge. Here, we demonstrate a tunable periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in a non-Hermitian interpolating Aubry-André-Fibonacci (IAAF) model by introducing an imaginary phase shift into the quasiperiodic potential. Such a periodic cascade of delocalization transitions arises from the competition between kinetic-energy-facilitated delocalization and gain-loss-regulated localization. In numerical static localization characterizations, successive regular stripe patterns for localized and extended states emerge in phase diagrams. We also derive an analytical expression for the cascade period and find that it relies solely on the imaginary phase shift. This provides a direct way of continuously tuning the cascade period via a single control parameter. Complementary static and dynamical diagnostics consistently confirm this periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in the non-Hermitian IAAF system. Our findings identify a novel class of delocalization transitions with tunable cascading periods, opening a route toward experimentally programmable control of delocalization.
summary: This work demonstrates a novel mechanism for controlling quantum localization by realizing a tunable, periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in a non-Hermitian model. By introducing an imaginary phase shift, the authors show that the cascade period can be precisely controlled, opening a pathway for experimentally programmable quantum control.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is achieving a programmable, tunable, and periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in a quantum system.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a tunable periodic cascade of delocalization transitions in the non-Hermitian IAAF model, with the cascade period analytically shown to depend solely on the imaginary phase shift.
method: The study employs static localization characterizations (phase diagrams) and dynamical diagnostics, including the Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR) and root-mean-square displacement ($\sigma(t)$), alongside analytical derivations.
model_or_system: The system is the non-Hermitian Interpolating Aubry-André-Fibonacci (IAAF) model. Non-Hermiticity is introduced via a complex on-site potential $V_k( eta)$ dependent on an imaginary phase shift ($\gamma$).
key_observables: Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), Root-Mean-Square Displacement ($\sigma(t)$), and the cascade period ($\Delta eta$).
important_parameters: The imaginary phase shift ($\gamma$), potential strength ($\lambda$), and the quasiperiodic modulation frequency ($\alpha$).
main_assumptions: The cascade period is analytically derived based on the poles of the potential, and the analysis relies on the competition between kinetic energy and gain-loss regulation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the complex potential profile in the $(	ext{U}, 	ext{W})$ plane, phase diagrams showing IPR vs. parameters, and time evolution plots of wave spreading ($\sigma(t)$) for both localized and extended states.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the non-Hermitian IAAF model and the concept of the cascade. It then uses static diagnostics (IPR) to map out phase diagrams. The core contribution involves deriving the analytical expression for the cascade period based on $\gamma$, which is confirmed by complementary dynamical measurements.
why_interesting: The tunable nature of the cascade period via a single parameter ($\gamma$) offers a direct, controllable mechanism for engineering quantum transport properties, which is highly relevant for designing quantum simulators or artificial lattices.
